kind: A pilot at full size, one seed: two variants of the looped stack against the loop as it was piloted, to pick the form of the loop's next full-length run.
why: full_size_loop_pilot left two questions open. Whether the loop needs the raised budget at full size: the looped stack was given 507,000 pulses a byte, 1.63 times the plain stack's, and on the test bed a loop at the old budget gained nothing; but at full size the raised budget alone made the plain stack 0.0093 worse, so the pulses themselves are not what helped. And whether the pool that lifts the ceiling adds to the loop: the loop's reads sit at their membrane's bound five times as often as the plain stack's (1.6% of their entries against 0.3%), and lifting removed all saturation from the plain stack at the same energy for a gain of 0.0064 at this rate (full_size_lifted_ceiling_pilot). The loop's full-length run (full_size_loop_run.json) trains the loop as piloted and does not wait for this. This pilot picks the form of the run after it.

arms.fs-loop6-b310: --stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 310000: the loop at the plain stack's budget, 17,200 pulses a byte for a level pass in place of 28,200
arms.fs-loop6-lift: --stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 507000 --pool-lifts-ceiling: the loop as piloted, under the pool that lifts the ceiling

base: fs-loop6 of full_size_loop_pilot (the loop with 507,000 pulses a byte and the plain pool: 1.31024), the same recipe, seed and code; beside it fs-st6 (the plain stack, 1.31985), fs-b507 (the plain stack with 507,000 pulses, 1.32913) and fs-st6-lift (the plain stack under the lifting pool, 1.31341)
training: full.sh KIND stack (v16's stack with forgetting slopes, windows of 512 bytes, batch 8, 24,000 updates, warmup 1,000, cosine over the run, seed 20001) at peak rate 6e-4 with each arm's flags; 34,810,900 parameters; code: the copy of 97a2772, as fs-loop6. Server GPU 0 in the window of 2026-11-24, each arm alone on the GPU, after the looped test-bed screen of skip_fibres_with_data.
measure: as full_size_loop_pilot: the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams after 8,192 unscored lead bytes, averaged weights, bits kept; each arm paired with fs-loop6 by experiments/gap_by_piece.py (near 496, far 8,192); the pulses a byte, the training time, and the share of membrane entries at their bound or cap (experiments/membrane_saturation.py, the first 65,536 validation bytes)
reading: One seed each: these readings pick a recipe and are not findings about the parts. The loop does not need the raised budget if fs-loop6-b310 is no more than 0.002 behind fs-loop6: the loop's next full-length run then trains at the old budget, the plain stack's energy. Further behind, the raised budget stays part of the loop. The lifting pool adds to the loop if fs-loop6-lift is at least 0.005 better than fs-loop6: the next full-length run then trains under it. Under 0.005 it is reported only. If both readings hold, the two changes are not known to combine, and a fourth arm (the old budget under the lifting pool) is piloted before either is adopted. Skip fibres join this pilot as an arm by an amendment if the looped screen of skip_fibres_with_data earns it. Recorded either way: every score, the gaps to fs-loop6 with their split by context, the pulses a byte, the time and the saturation of each arm.
seen_before_recording: full_size_loop_pilot's and full_size_lifted_ceiling_pilot's results. No looped stack has trained at full size at the old budget or under the lifting pool. On the test bed, stack_loop/preregistered.json (a loop at the old budget within the plain seeds, at 3e-4 and 6,000 updates) and loop_with_data's runs so far (at 6,000 updates the loop 1.60491 against its energy control 1.63019 and the base 1.62828; the control at 24,000 updates 1.48591 against the base's 1.48247). The loop's full-length run is queued and has not started. Launch checks on the server's CPU at a width of 64: the loop under the lifting pool trains 30 updates and is scored.

amendment.change: Before any run of this record. A third arm: fs-loop12-lift, --stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 507000 --pool-lifts-ceiling at peak rate 1.2e-3, otherwise as fs-loop6-lift, on GPU 1 after the full-size pilot of a third loop pass (full_size_loop_passes.json). Its reading: the lifted loop gains from the Transformer's rate if fs-loop12-lift is at least 0.005 better than fs-loop6-lift with the paired interval clear of zero; the loop's next full-length run then trains at 1.2e-3 if it trains under the lifting pool. Within 0.003 the rate stays 6e-4; between, unclear and reported. The other two arms and their readings are unchanged.
amendment.why: The full-size pair found that a faster rate pays the Transformer and hardly pays the stack once both have seen all their data: 0.028 for the Transformer from 1.2e-3 against 0.004 for the plain stack from 6e-4 after 90,000 updates, and in the pair's own validation readings the gap keeps growing by 0.024 with each doubling of training where at a shared rate of 3e-4 it stops growing after about 48,000 updates (full_size_best_rate_pair.json, pair_curves.json). At 1.2e-3 the plain stack's membranes saturate, and the pool that lifts the ceiling removes that, so that the lifted stack at 1.2e-3 matched the plain stack's best after 24,000 updates (full_size_lifted_ceiling_pilot.json). Whether the loop under the lifting pool gains from the Transformer's rate decides at which rate the loop's next full-length run trains, and no arm asks it.
amendment.seen_before_amendment: No arm of this record has trained. The full-size pair's result and the pair's validation curves; fsp-loop at 49,500 of 90,000 updates and unscored.
